transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-08-12
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Rita Patel (Echo Head of ML), Samir Gupta (SRE), Lena Wu (Product), Marcus Reed (Data Eng)

Summary: Quick weekly POC sync focused on KV/prefix cache hit-rate gains from last week's heuristic changes, prompt reuse canonicalization, and next steps to run a full prod-sim benchmark. Customer asked clarifying security questions around VPC and KMS for Dedicated.

Topics: 1) numbers from last 7 days (hitrate uplift) 2) prefetch tuning and eviction thresholds 3) prompt normalization strategy 4) latency/cost tradeoffs 5) security/deploy preference and next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: okay hi everyone, uh thanks for joining, we have the usual agenda, quick numbers then tuning notes and next steps. Rita you ok?
[00:32] Rita: yeah thanks Maya, sorry about the timing, we had an incident morning, should be fine. excited to see the hit rate changes.
[01:05] Diego: quick note before numbers — we pushed the relaxed prefix matching and a headroom prefetch heuristic on Tuesday evening. so two changes: broader prefix grouping and a small prefetch window for session-affine keys.
[01:40] Samir: when you say prefetch window like how many keys? what's the memory cost?
[02:05] Diego: currently it's 8 keys per session by default, honoring your memory cap. on our cluster sim it used +12% peak RAM per worker, but reduced downstream requests by about 24%.
[02:48] Lena: do we have the raw numbers on hit rate uplift? we saw a spike in our dashboard but want to confirm.
[03:10] Diego: yes, raw: baseline KV hit rate was 38% for canonicalized prefixes; after the prefix grouping change we went to 48% first 24h and after enabling prefetch to 52% steady state. caveat — metrics noise from weekend traffic, but that's the trend.
[03:48] Rita: 52% is great. is that across all models or just the 7B family?
[04:10] Diego: primarily with the 7B variant you're running, we did a small check on 13B and saw similar relative gains but absolute hit rates were slightly lower — around 45% to 49% post-change.
[04:38] Marcus: any latency impact per-request when prefetching? our p95 is pretty sensitive.
[05:02] Diego: good question — at our infra settings prefetch adds about 10-18ms to the initial request if it triggers synchronous prefetch; with async background prefetching we see negligible added tail unless eviction thrash happens. tradeoff is slightly higher per-node CPU.
[05:32] Samir: that 10-18ms is acceptable if token cost drops enough. do you have cost delta numbers?
[05:58] Maya: quick ballpark — for Echo's workload, reducing remote decode calls due to higher KV hit rate dropped estimated token compute by ~14% which maps to about a 9-11% cost reduction at current rates. we'll follow up with a precise sheet.
[06:32] Lena: on prompt reuse — we still see high variability because product team drops a lot of dynamic context. how do you recommend canonicalizing?
[07:00] Diego: two levers: structural templating (move non-essential user strings to separate metadata fields) and fuzzy normalization for dates/names (e.g., map to <DATE> tokens). plus we can build a small lightweight rewrite layer at the edge to collapse near-duplicates before they hit the KV keying.
[07:34] Rita: are there cases where normalization reduces quality for us? we worry about losing nuance.
[07:56] Diego: yes sometimes, especially with slot-based prompts where wording matters. recommended approach: start with a conservative canonicalization set (emails, timestamps, uuids) and run A/B quality checks on 5-10k prompts to validate.
[08:26] Maya: note — Diego will run the A/B quality check as part of the bench run if Echo supplies the sanitized prompt corpus.
[08:52] Marcus: on eviction policy — you mentioned we should tune TTLs for user sessions. what's the guidance?
[09:12] Diego: for your workload we recommend session TTL of 12 minutes with a soft eviction threshold when global mem usage hits 80% and aggressive LRU beyond 90%. this preserves session affinity while preventing thrash in high-load bursts.
[09:44] Samir: curious about multi-tenant isolation — we're leaning to Dedicated VPC for compliance. what extra security pieces are required?
[10:07] Maya: with Dedicated you get VPC peering, optional private control plane, and KMS integration. we also offer SOC 2 docs, audit logs, and SAML SSO integrations. I'll attach the security packet after the call.
[10:38] Rita: acceptable. is the Dedicated latency better or worse vs hosted?
[10:58] Diego: latency mostly depends on network topology; Dedicated in your region with GPU pools we recommended usually reduces WAN variability, sometimes shaving 5-25ms off p95 compared to multi-tenant hosted endpoints. but cost is higher and commit terms apply.
[11:30] Lena: on the pilot -- we need clearer pass/fail criteria. Rita, what would success look like in 6 weeks?
[11:50] Rita: primary: 50%+ KV/prefix hit rate on our production traffic, second: sustain p95 latency under 220ms, and third: verified security posture (SAML + KMS) in place.
[12:16] Maya: perfect — aligning to that. Diego, do you think the bench will show 50%+ if they send the corpus?
[12:34] Diego: yes there's a good chance. our sim hit rate exceeded 50% with current heuristics on a 30k sample; real production will vary but with prompt normalization and TTL tuning we should hit the target.
[12:58] Samir: can we also have a traffic-sliced benchmark — e.g., new users vs returning — to see hit rate skew?
[13:20] Diego: absolutely, plan to split the trace into cohorts and show per-cohort hit rates.
[13:40] Lena: you mentioned prefetch memory cost earlier — can we put a cap and do adaptive prefetch?
[13:58] Diego: yes adaptive prefetch based on observed session reuse works well. it starts small and grows when reuse is detected, shrink when not. we'll include adaptive in the bench.
[14:20] Rita: anything else about prompt rewriting — do you support a map table for known synonyms?
[14:38] Diego: yes we can optionally add a canonicalization mapping for common product synonyms to reduce key cardinality. that's a small ruleset we can maintain with Echo's product team.
[15:00] Maya: okay quick status check on outstanding items from last week: Marcus had the API token rotation question?
[15:18] Marcus: yes we rotated tokens and noticed a small uptick in 401 errors because some long-lived sessions didn't refresh. resolved by shortening token TTL and adding graceful refresh.
[15:40] Maya: thanks — good catch.
[15:52] Samir: on the security packet, I want to make sure HSM/KMS integration works with our internal key policies. any caveats?
[16:12] Maya: Redwood supports customer-managed keys; our Private deployment can integrate with your HSM, but we need the security team to sign off. I'll cc security in the follow-up email.
[16:36] Rita: any blockers from Redwood side for running the prod-sim bench?
[16:52] Diego: none — just the sanitized prompt set and the 30k request trace you mentioned. also we need a target SLA for the bench (e.g., same concurrency as prod).
[17:12] Lena: we'll send the trace and a concurrency target.
[17:26] Diego: great. next: quality monitoring — we can run automatic evals on the bench to detect regressions after canonicalization. that would output a regression delta per prompt family.
[17:56] Rita: that will be very helpful.
[18:10] Maya: reminder — for Dedicated discussion, I'll include pricing tiers. for now Pilot continues on Hosted but we are tracking Dedicated interest.
[18:30] Marcus: timeline — when can Dedicated be provisioned if we go that route?
[18:46] Diego: typical lead time is 2-4 weeks for initial Dedicated config in-region, depending on capacity.
[19:05] Samir: ok. can Diego share the config template for memory limits and prefetch parameters?
[19:22] Diego: yes I'll paste that into the sheet.
[19:40] Lena: any anomalies in logs this week tied to the heuristic change?
[19:58] Diego: we saw an increase in soft misses while TTL ramped but no errors; overall request success remained steady. we fixed a small bug where key canonicalization dropped trailing punctuation in some edge cases.
[20:20] Rita: oh that might explain a few misses we saw. thanks for fixing.
[20:36] Maya: quick housekeeping — I'll add links: pilot spreadsheet (https://docs.redwood/pilot-echo-2026), security packet (https://redwood.docs/security/evaluations), bench template (https://docs.redwood/bench/template).
[21:00] Marcus: got it.
[21:12] Diego: final note: we'll include per-model breakdown (7B vs 13B) and per-cohort slices in the bench output.
[21:32] Rita: excellent.
[21:45] Maya: ok wrapping up — recap and next steps.
[22:00] Maya: recap: 1) Diego runs full prod-sim bench with cohorts and adaptive prefetch, includes A/B tests for prompt normalization, and posts results; 2) Maya shares Dedicated vs Hosted cost delta and security docs; 3) Echo shares sanitized prompts and trace; 4) next sync 2026-08-19 to review results.
[22:36] Lena: one last thing — can we include a quick demo of the rewrite layer soon? maybe after bench?
[22:58] Diego: yes we can demo the rewrite in a 20-min focused session after bench results.
[23:15] Maya: great. thanks everyone, see you next week.

End of transcript.
